newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says will not use force if rebel arms laid down.
newsitem.headline: Peru says will not use force if rebel arms laid down.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori said on Saturday the Peruvian government will not use force against Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels if they lay down their weapons and release all hostages.

"The proposal is concrete. That the captors lay down the weapons to a guarantor committee and that they allow the evacuation of all the hostages without exception," Fujimori said in his first public statement since the crisis began.

"In this way the possibility of the use of force by the Peruvian state will be ruled out and from there, with all guarantees, a way out can be studied. This is the proposal of the government before the country and the international community."
Fujimori, who spoke rapidly and firmly, was giving his first public statement on the crisis since MRTA rebels took over the Japanese ambassador's residence last Tuesday night.
He also condemned the rebels for their "repugnant attack against the freedom, health and life of innocent people."

"Although it seems incredible with this act of terror and flagrant violation of human rights, the so-called MRTA, the same that in the last decade was sowing destruction and death in Peru ... hopes to start a dialogue that leads to a peace accord. That is to say, they hope for dialogue by placing an AKM rifle on the neck of hostages."

Fujimori added that his government "is not prepared to accept the force and violence (that) a terrorist command imposes on 23 million peopole, who reject these methods, which are neither civilized or political.
"We cannot talk of peace or accord while terror is used as the main argument."
Fujimori said that since the crisis began the government had put into practice a secret emergency strategy "with the objective of avoiding bloodshed."
He said the government's aim was to find a solution that did not breach the human rights either of the hostages or the rebels.
There was no immediate response from the rebels, who earlier were in contact with local media via walkie-talkie.
